ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ and $E$ are points on sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, with $DE \parallel BC$. If $\frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\text{quadrilateral } DBCE}} = 1:8$, what is the value of $\frac{DE}{BC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the ratio of the area of $\triangle ADE$ to the area of quadrilateral DBCE is $1:8$, \\
it follows that the area of $\triangle ADE$ is $\frac{1}{9}$ the area of $\triangle ABC$, \\
thus $\frac{{S}_{\triangle ADE}}{{S}_{\triangle ABC}}=\frac{1}{9}$. \\
Since $DE \parallel BC$, \\
then $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$, \\
thus $\frac{{S}_{\triangle ADE}}{{S}_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{DE}{BC}\right)^{2}$, \\
hence $\left(\frac{DE}{BC}\right)^{2}=\frac{1}{9}$, \\
therefore $\frac{DE}{BC}=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$.

Point D is located on side AB, point E is located on side AC, line segment DE connects D and E, and from the figure it seems that DE is parallel to the base BC. Reasoning: Because DE ∥ BC, and D is on AB and E is on AC, △ADE and △ABC are similar. It is known that S_{△ADE} : S_{quadrilateral DBCE} = 1 : 8, and the whole △ABC is composed of △ADE and quadrilateral DBCE, so S_{△ADE} : S_{△ABC} = 1 : (1+8) = 1 : 9, that is, S_{△ADE}/S_{△ABC} = 1/9. The ratio of the areas of similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths, and the corresponding sides are DE and BC, therefore (DE/BC)^2 = 1/9. Since the side length ratio is positive, obtain DE/BC = 1/3.
